number.why: The counts support a reconstructed RR of (61/180)/(75/180) = 0.8133333333, but do not establish that RR for the served in-hospital/index-admission window. The registry explicitly specifies postoperative AF incidence at 3 months; the abstract does not bind these counts to an in-hospital window. Recording this discrepancy without changing confirmation is insufficient. The full randomized denominators support the reconstruction, but the packet does not explicitly identify these results as intention-to-treat. The published 95% CI is for an absolute difference, not the reconstructed RR.

postoperative AF (colchicine, 61 patients [33.9%]; placebo, 75 patients [41.7%]; absolute difference, 7.8%; 95% CI, -2.2% to 17.6%)

PROTOCOL PRIMARY OUTCOME: Post-pericardiotomy syndrome, post-operative effusions, post-operative atrial fibrillation incidence | Incidence of the outcomes at 3 months from cardiac surgery | TIME FRAME: 3 months

entry.why: Adult cardiac-surgery eligibility and perioperative colchicine versus placebo are established. The population is restricted to patients in sinus rhythm and excludes cardiac transplantation; these restrictions do not defeat entry for the packet's broad question.

quotes.span: Inclusion Criteria: * Age \> 18years * Candidate to cardiac surgery but cardiac transplantation * Informed consent
Main exclusion criteria were absence of sinus rhythm at enrollment, cardiac transplantation, and contraindications to colchicine.

INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to receive placebo (n=180) or colchicine (0.5 mg twice daily in patients ≥70 kg or 0.5 mg once daily in patients <70 kg; n=180) starting between 48 and 72 hours before surgery and continued for 1 month after surgery.

missed: The consequential issue is the unsupported assertion that the timepoint defect has no effect on number validity: valid aggregate counts cannot confirm an effect for a different observation window. No replacement in-hospital RR can be established from this packet.
